title: 1 Kings Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 11.

questions.question: Which foreign women did King Solomon love according to 1 Kings 11?
options: Daughter of Pharaoh, Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, Hittites
questions.correctAnswer: Daughter of Pharaoh, Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, Hittites
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:1 states Solomon loved many strange women, including the daughter of Pharaoh and women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Zidonians, and Hittites.

questions.question: What warning did the LORD give concerning the nations Solomon married women from?
options: They would turn away the heart of Israel after their gods
They would bring great wealth to Israel
They would help Solomon build a temple
They would aid Israel in battle
questions.correctAnswer: They would turn away the heart of Israel after their gods
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:2 explains that the LORD said these nations would turn away the heart of Israel after their gods.

questions.question: How many wives and concubines did Solomon have?
options: Seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines
One hundred wives and fifty concubines
Three hundred wives and seven hundred concubines
Five hundred wives and two hundred concubines
questions.correctAnswer: Seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:3 states Solomon had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon's heart remained perfect with the LORD as David's heart was.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:4 says Solomon's heart was not perfect with the LORD as David's heart was because his wives turned him after other gods.

questions.question: After which gods did Solomon go according to 1 Kings 11?
questions.correctAnswer: Ashtoreth and Milcom
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:5 specifies Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon fully followed the LORD just as David did.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:6 states Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD and did not fully follow the LORD as David did.

questions.question: Which high places did Solomon build for foreign gods near Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Chemosh and Molech
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:7 records Solomon built high places for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, and Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.

questions.question: What did Solomon’s strange wives do that Solomon also allowed?
options: Burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:8 states Solomon's strange wives burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD was pleased with Solomon's heart because he obeyed fully.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:9 shows that the LORD was angry with Solomon because his heart was turned from the LORD God of Israel.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give Solomon that he did not keep?
options: Not to go after other gods
To build a temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Not to go after other gods
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:10 states that the LORD commanded Solomon not to go after other gods, but he did not keep this command.

questions.question: What consequence did the LORD say would happen because Solomon did not keep His covenant?
options: The kingdom would be torn from Solomon and given to his servant
Solomon would build more high places
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom would be torn from Solomon and given to his servant
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:11 reveals the LORD would rend the kingdom from Solomon and give it to his servant because he broke the covenant.

questions.question: Who was stirred up by the LORD as an adversary against Solomon?
questions.correctAnswer: Hadad the Edomite
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:14 states the LORD stirred up Hadad the Edomite as an adversary to Solomon.

questions.question: Where did Hadad flee to as a child after Joab killed the males in Edom?
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:17 shows Hadad fled with certain Edomites to Egypt as a child.

questions.question: Who did Pharaoh give Hadad to wife in Egypt?
options: The sister of Tahpenes the queen
questions.correctAnswer: The sister of Tahpenes the queen
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:19 states Pharaoh gave Hadad the sister of Tahpenes the queen to wife.

questions.question: In 1 Kings 11, which event happens first?
options: Solomon builds high places for foreign gods
God stirs up Hadad the Edomite as an adversary
Solomon's wives turn his heart away
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon's wives turn his heart away
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:3-4 shows Solomon's wives turned his heart away first before the LORD stirred up adversaries (1 Kings 11:14) and Jeroboam's prophecy (1 Kings 11:29).

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How long did Joab remain in Edom with all Israel after smiting every male, according to 1 Kings 11?
questions.correctAnswer: Six months
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:16 states that Joab remained in Edom for six months until he had cut off every male, showing the duration of the military campaign.

questions.question: Where did Hadad the Edomite flee to as a child after David's campaign in Edom?
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:17 explains that Hadad fled to Egypt as a child with certain Edomites after Joab's campaign, highlighting his exile.

questions.question: What land did Pharaoh give to Hadad when he came to Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: A house and land
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 11:18, Pharaoh gave Hadad a house, victuals (food), and land, showing Pharaoh's favor towards him.

questions.question: Who did Pharaoh give to Hadad as a wife?
options: The sister of Tahpenes the queen
questions.correctAnswer: The sister of Tahpenes the queen
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:19 states that Hadad married the sister of Pharaoh's wife, who was the sister of Tahpenes the queen, indicating a political alliance.

questions.question: Where was Genubath, the son of Hadad, raised?
questions.correctAnswer: In Pharaoh's household
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:20 explains that Genubath was weaned and raised in Pharaoh's household, showing his integration into Egyptian royalty.

questions.question: What was Hadad's request to Pharaoh after he heard about David's death?
options: To return to his own country
questions.correctAnswer: To return to his own country
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:21 records Hadad's request to Pharaoh to depart and return to his own country after hearing David had died.

questions.question: What was Pharaoh's initial reaction to Hadad's request to leave Egypt?
options: He questioned what Hadad lacked with him
He sent Hadad away with gifts
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned what Hadad lacked with him
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 11:22, Pharaoh asked Hadad what he lacked with him, showing reluctance about letting him go.

questions.question: Who was the other adversary God stirred up against Solomon besides Hadad?
questions.correctAnswer: Rezon, son of Eliadah
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 11:23, God also stirred up Rezon, son of Eliadah, as an adversary to Solomon, demonstrating God's judgment.

questions.question: Where did Rezon establish his reign after fleeing from Hadadezer king of Zobah?
questions.correctAnswer: Damascus
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:24 records that Rezon gathered men, became captain over a band, and reigned in Damascus, opposing Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Rezon was an adversary to Israel only for a short time during Solomon's reign.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:25 states Rezon was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, showing a prolonged opposition.

questions.question: What was the name of Jeroboam's mother?
questions.correctAnswer: Zeruah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:26 identifies Jeroboam's mother as Zeruah, a widow woman, indicating his family background.

questions.question: What construction project of Solomon's caused Jeroboam to rebel?
options: Millo and repairing breaches in the city of David
questions.correctAnswer: Millo and repairing breaches in the city of David
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:27 shows that Jeroboam rebelled partly because Solomon built Millo and repaired breaches in the city of David.

questions.question: What position did Solomon give Jeroboam because of his industriousness?
options: Ruler over the house of Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: Ruler over the house of Joseph
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:28 states that Solomon made Jeroboam ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph due to his valor and industriousness.

questions.question: Where did the prophet Ahijah meet Jeroboam and what was unique about Ahijah's garment?
options: In Jerusalem; it was old and torn
In the field; it was new
In the temple; it was embroidered
questions.correctAnswer: In the field; it was new
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:29 notes Ahijah met Jeroboam in the field, and Ahijah was wearing a new garment, setting up a prophetic act.

questions.question: True or False: Ahijah tore his new garment into twelve pieces to symbolize the division of the kingdom.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:30 records that Ahijah tore his new garment into twelve pieces, symbolizing the twelve tribes and the future kingdom split.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 11.

questions.question: What was the reason given for God deciding to rend the kingdom from Solomon and give it to his servant?
options: Because Solomon did not build the temple properly
Because Solomon did not keep God's covenant and statutes
Because Solomon was defeated in battle
Because Solomon refused to marry foreign wives
questions.correctAnswer: Because Solomon did not keep God's covenant and statutes
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:11 states that God was displeased because Solomon did not keep His covenant and statutes, which is why He decided to rend the kingdom from him.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 11, how many tribes would Jeroboam receive when the kingdom was divided?
questions.correctAnswer: Ten tribes
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:31 clearly states that Jeroboam was to take ten pieces of the kingdom, signifying ten tribes would be given to him.

questions.question: Why was one tribe reserved for Solomon's son, according to God's promise?
options: For the sake of David, God's servant, and Jerusalem
Because Solomon's son was the strongest warrior
As a punishment to Solomon's son
Because Solomon requested it in his prayers
questions.correctAnswer: For the sake of David, God's servant, and Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:32 explains that one tribe would be kept for Solomon's son for David's sake and for Jerusalem, the city God chose among all tribes.

questions.question: Which gods did Solomon and Israel worship that caused God to forsake them, as mentioned in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:33 states these specific gods were worshipped, causing Israel to forsake God and His ways.

questions.question: What assurance did God give Jeroboam if he obeyed all His commandments and statutes?
options: That he would build a sure house like David's and reign over Israel
That he would conquer Egypt and Assyria
That he would become a prophet
That he would rule over all twelve tribes
questions.correctAnswer: That he would build a sure house like David's and reign over Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:38 promises Jeroboam that if he obeyed God, He would build him a sure house as for David and give Israel to him.

questions.question: What was God's declared attitude toward the seed of David due to Solomon's sin?
options: He would afflict them, but not forever
questions.correctAnswer: He would afflict them, but not forever
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:39 shows God would afflict David's seed due to Solomon's sins, but His punishment was not eternal.

questions.question: Who did Solomon seek to kill after God's announcement about the kingdom division, causing that person to flee to Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeroboam
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 11:40, Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam, which led Jeroboam to flee to Egypt.

questions.question: How long did Solomon reign over all Israel according to this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty years
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:42 states that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.

questions.question: Who succeeded Solomon as king after his death?
questions.correctAnswer: Rehoboam, his son
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:43 records that Rehoboam, Solomon's son, reigned in his stead after Solomon died.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book contains a similar promise about the division of the kingdom and the preservation of David’s line, complementing 1 Kings 11?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Samuel 7
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7 contains God's covenant promise to David about his lineage and kingdom, complementing the theme of God's covenant in 1 Kings 11:34-36.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'rend' as used in the context 'I will rend the kingdom out of his hand' in 1 Kings 11:31?
options: To tear apart or divide forcibly
questions.correctAnswer: To tear apart or divide forcibly
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'rend' (Hebrew: 'kara') means to tear or rend forcibly, indicating the division of the kingdom as described in 1 Kings 11:31.

questions.question: What literary device is evident when Ahijah tears his new garment into twelve pieces to symbolize the division of the kingdom?
questions.correctAnswer: Symbolism
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:30 shows Ahijah’s tearing of the new garment as a symbolic act representing the kingdom's division, a clear use of symbolism.

questions.question: True or False: God promised to remove all the tribes from Solomon's son and give them entirely to Jeroboam.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:34-36 explains that God would not take the whole kingdom but leave one tribe for Solomon’s son for David’s sake and Jerusalem’s sake.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam was made ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph before he rebelled against Solomon.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:28 states that Solomon made Jeroboam ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph before Jeroboam lifted up his hand against Solomon.

questions.question: Which adversary was raised by God against Solomon and was a king over Syria, abhorred Israel, and reigned in Damascus?
questions.correctAnswer: Rezon son of Eliadah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:23-25 describes Rezon as an adversary to Israel who reigned in Damascus and abhorred Israel.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological principle is demonstrated by Solomon's failure to keep God's command regarding foreign wives and gods?
options: God's covenant demands exclusive worship and obedience
God desires cultural assimilation of all nations
Solomon was justified in marrying many wives for political alliances
God rewards disobedience with increased blessings
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant demands exclusive worship and obedience
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:9-10 shows the LORD's anger because Solomon's heart turned from Him, violating the command not to follow other gods, demonstrating the theological principle that God's covenant requires exclusive worship and obedience.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by God's promise to not take the entire kingdom from Solomon during his lifetime but to do so in his son's days?
options: God's faithfulness to His covenant promises despite human failure
God's immediate judgment upon all sin
The doctrine of predestination without regard to human actions
God's indifference to the sins of rulers
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness to His covenant promises despite human failure
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:11-13 explains that God will rend the kingdom because Solomon broke the covenant, but not during his reign for David's sake, showing God's faithfulness to His covenant despite Solomon's sin.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 11:5 and 1 Kings 11:7 collectively reveal the seriousness of idolatry in God's eyes?
options: Idolatry involves pursuing false gods and building high places for them, which God abhors
Idolatry encourages cultural diversity and religious tolerance
Idolatry is acceptable if it is done privately without public worship
Idolatry is only a problem when it affects political alliances
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry involves pursuing false gods and building high places for them, which God abhors
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 7 show Solomon's pursuit of Ashtoreth, Milcom, Chemosh, and Molech—false gods—and his building of high places for them, highlighting that idolatry is serious rebellion against God.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by His decision to raise adversaries against Solomon (Hadad and Rezon) as found in this chapter?
options: God's justice in punishing covenant unfaithfulness
God's mercy in forgiving all sins immediately
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice in punishing covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:14-25 records God stirring up adversaries against Solomon, showing divine justice responding to Solomon's covenant breach.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Jeroboam’s rise and prophecy from Ahijah (1 Kings 11:26-38) contribute to the biblical theology of divine election and judgment?
options: It shows God electing leaders to execute judgment on unfaithful rulers
It teaches that human ambition alone determines kingship
It supports the idea that rebellion is always unjustified
It reveals that God does not interfere in political affairs
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God electing leaders to execute judgment on unfaithful rulers
questions.explanation: Verses 29-38 depict Ahijah’s prophecy that Jeroboam will rule ten tribes, illustrating God’s sovereign election for judgment against Solomon’s disobedience.

questions.question: What synthesis about divine holiness and human responsibility emerges from 1 Kings 11:1-3 and 1 Kings 11:9-11?
options: God requires holiness from His people, and human disobedience leads to covenant judgment
God permits syncretism if it benefits the kingdom politically
Human responsibility is irrelevant to divine blessings
God overlooks disobedience when kings are wise
questions.correctAnswer: God requires holiness from His people, and human disobedience leads to covenant judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 show Solomon's disobedience through foreign wives and idolatry; verses 9-11 show God's anger and covenant judgment, emphasizing holiness and responsibility.

questions.question: Which theological insight is taught by the fact that God will afflict the seed of David but not forever as stated in 1 Kings 11:39?
options: God’s discipline is corrective, not ultimately destructive
God rejects the Davidic line permanently
God’s promises are conditional and easily withdrawn
God shows no mercy to covenant breakers
questions.correctAnswer: God’s discipline is corrective, not ultimately destructive
questions.explanation: Verse 39 states God will afflict David’s seed but not forever, indicating corrective discipline, consistent with God's covenantal mercy.

questions.question: What does the episode of Hadad the Edomite (1 Kings 11:14-22) reveal about God's providence and sovereignty over nations?
options: God sovereignly raises enemies to accomplish His purposes
God only cares about Israel and ignores other nations
God allows evil without control over it
God's providence is limited to the Promised Land
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly raises enemies to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 14-22 show God stirring Hadad as an adversary, demonstrating divine sovereignty over nations for His purposes.

questions.question: How does Solomon's heart turning after other gods (1 Kings 11:4-6) contrast with David's heart, and what doctrine does this contrast illustrate?
options: The doctrine of faithfulness and the consequences of spiritual decline
The doctrine of eternal security regardless of conduct
The doctrine of predestination without human response
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of faithfulness and the consequences of spiritual decline
questions.explanation: Verses 4-6 contrast Solomon's unfaithfulness with David's perfect heart, illustrating the importance of faithfulness and the consequences of turning away from God.

questions.question: What apologetic challenge does 1 Kings 11:40 address regarding God's justice in the history of Solomon and Jeroboam?
options: Sceptics claim God's promises contradict His actions; this passage shows God’s righteous judgment and mercy coexist
Sceptics claim God is unjust in judgment; this passage shows God punishes without cause
Sceptics claim God ignores sin; this passage shows God is indifferent
Sceptics claim God arbitrarily chooses kings; this passage shows human politics determine outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: Sceptics claim God's promises contradict His actions; this passage shows God’s righteous judgment and mercy coexist
questions.explanation: Verse 40 shows Solomon seeking to kill Jeroboam, who flees to Egypt, fulfilling prophecy and demonstrating God’s just judgment alongside His merciful timing, addressing sceptical objections.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 11:8 teach about the influence of idolatrous practices on Israel’s leadership and worship?
options: Foreign wives led Solomon to permit their incense and sacrifices, corrupting true worship
Idolatrous practices were tolerated as long as Israelite gods were worshiped
Solomon expelled all foreign worship practices immediately
Idolatry was encouraged by the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Foreign wives led Solomon to permit their incense and sacrifices, corrupting true worship
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states Solomon built high places for his wives' gods and allowed incense and sacrifices, showing the corrupting influence on worship.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted by His appearance to Solomon twice and His command to not follow other gods, as mentioned in 1 Kings 11:9?
options: God’s patience and revelation of His will
questions.correctAnswer: God’s patience and revelation of His will
questions.explanation: Verse 9 mentions God appeared twice to Solomon and commanded exclusive worship, showing God's patient revelation and expectation of obedience.

questions.question: How does the division of the kingdom into ten tribes for Jeroboam and one tribe for Solomon's son (1 Kings 11:31-36) reflect God's covenantal justice and mercy?
options: God executes justice by judgment but preserves mercy for David’s line
God completely rejects the Davidic covenant
God arbitrarily divides the kingdom without purpose
God shows no concern for political stability
questions.correctAnswer: God executes justice by judgment but preserves mercy for David’s line
questions.explanation: Verses 31-36 describe God rending the kingdom due to sin but sparing one tribe for David's sake, combining justice with mercy.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 11:28 reveal about Solomon's use of human gifts and the potential spiritual danger therein?
options: Even industriousness and leadership gifts can lead to pride and disobedience
Leadership is unrelated to spiritual responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: Even industriousness and leadership gifts can lead to pride and disobedience
questions.explanation: Verse 28 notes Jeroboam’s industriousness and Solomon's favor, yet Jeroboam later rebels, illustrating that gifts do not ensure spiritual obedience.

questions.question: How does the fate of Hadad and Rezon as adversaries to Solomon illustrate God's use of human history in the redemptive narrative?
options: God sovereignly uses political adversaries to fulfill covenantal promises and discipline
God is powerless in human political affairs
Adversaries act independently of God's will
God only works through Israelite kings
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly uses political adversaries to fulfill covenantal promises and discipline
questions.explanation: Verses 14-25 show Hadad and Rezon rising against Solomon, demonstrating God's sovereign orchestration of history in judgment and redemption.
